c.x: A free front-end framework for faster and easier web development
A paid back-end framework for building database-driven web servers
A free server-side language for processing data sent from forms
A browser extension that makes web pages load faster for visitors

qs.e: Bootstrap is a free front-end framework (HTML, CSS, and JavaScript) for developing responsive, mobile-first websites faster and more easily.

qs.q: Which statement best describes what Bootstrap provides?

c.x: Server scripts for forms, buttons and tables, plus optional database plugins
Design templates for typography, forms, buttons and tables, plus mandatory JavaScript plugins
Design templates for typography, forms, buttons and tables, plus optional JavaScript plugins
Design templates for desktop pages only, plus optional JavaScript plugins

qs.e: Bootstrap includes HTML- and CSS-based design templates for typography, forms, buttons, tables, images and more, and it also offers <u>optional</u> JavaScript plugins. It also makes it easy to create responsive designs.

c.x: Building sites that load faster by compressing all of their images
Building sites that automatically adjust to look good on all devices
Building sites that respond only to mouse clicks and key presses
Building separate versions of a site for each device manufacturer

qs.e: Responsive web design is about creating web sites which automatically adjust themselves to look good on all devices, from small phones to large desktops.

qs.q: A team with only <u>basic</u> HTML and CSS knowledge must build a site that works in Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari and Opera. Which two advantages of Bootstrap help them most?

c.x: Mobile-first approach and responsive features
Easy to use and mobile-first approach
Responsive features and browser compatibility
Easy to use and browser compatibility

qs.e: Easy to use: anybody with just basic knowledge of HTML and CSS can start using Bootstrap. Browser compatibility: Bootstrap is compatible with all modern browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Internet Explorer, Edge, Safari, and Opera).

qs.q: Which option correctly matches an advantage of Bootstrap with its description?

c.x: Responsive features — the CSS adjusts to phones, tablets and desktops
Mobile-first approach — the CSS adjusts to phones, tablets and desktops
Browser compatibility — anybody with basic HTML and CSS can start using it
Easy to use — mobile-first styles are part of the core framework

qs.e: Responsive features: Bootstrap's responsive CSS adjusts to phones, tablets, and desktops. Mobile-first approach: mobile-first styles are part of the core framework. Easy to use refers to basic HTML and CSS knowledge being enough, and browser compatibility refers to working in all modern browsers.

qs.q: Which statement about Bootstrap 5 is correct according to the lecture?

c.x: It is the oldest version, kept for older browsers with fewer components
It is the newest version, but it supports only one major browser and platform
It is the newest version, with new components, faster style sheets and more responsiveness
It is the newest version, but it removes responsive design to run faster

qs.e: Bootstrap 5 is the newest version, with new components, faster style sheets, and more responsiveness. It supports the latest, stable releases of all major browsers and platforms.

qs.q: What is the main difference between Bootstrap 5 and Bootstrap 3 & 4?

c.x: Bootstrap 5 uses jQuery instead of plain JavaScript
Bootstrap 5 uses plain JavaScript instead of jQuery
Bootstrap 5 drops HTML templates and keeps only CSS files
Bootstrap 5 works only on desktops and not on phones

qs.e: The main difference stated in the lecture is that Bootstrap 5 switched to JavaScript instead of jQuery, while Bootstrap 3 and 4 depend on jQuery.

qs.q: According to the lecture, what is true about the mobile-first approach in Bootstrap 3?

c.x: Mobile-first styles are an optional add-on that is installed separately
Mobile-first styles work only when Bootstrap is used through a CDN
Mobile-first styles are part of the core framework itself
Mobile-first styles apply only to tablets and not to phones

qs.e: In Bootstrap 3, mobile-first styles are part of the core framework — they do not need a separate add-on.

qs.q: Which two ways does the lecture give for starting to use Bootstrap on your own website?

c.x: Buy a license from getbootstrap.com, or include it from a CDN
Download it from getbootstrap.com, or include it from a CDN
Download it from getbootstrap.com, or write it from scratch in CSS
Copy it from a browser's cache, or include it from a CDN

qs.e: Bootstrap is completely free. You can either download it from getbootstrap.com and link the files in your HTML, or include it from a CDN.

qs.q: What does CDN stand for, and why is it used to include Bootstrap?

c.x: Content Display Network — it is the quickest way to get started
Content Delivery Network — it requires downloading all files first
Content Delivery Network — it is the quickest way to get started
Code Distribution Node — it is the quickest way to get started

qs.e: CDN means Content Delivery Network. Including Bootstrap through a CDN is the quickest way to get started, because you only copy the CSS link and the JavaScript script tag from the official Bootstrap documentation instead of downloading files.

qs.q: When including Bootstrap through a CDN, where should the CSS link and the JavaScript bundle be placed?

c.x: Both the CSS link and the JavaScript bundle in the `<head>`
CSS link before the closing `</body>`; JavaScript bundle in the `<head>`
Both the CSS link and the JavaScript bundle before the closing `</body>`
CSS link in the `<head>`; JavaScript bundle before the closing `</body>`

qs.e: Copy the CSS `<link>` into the `<head>`, and the JavaScript bundle (including Popper.js) `<script>` tag before the closing `</body>` tag, as given in the official Bootstrap documentation.

qs.q:
Study the CDN example:
```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://maxcdn.bootstrapcdn.com/bootstrap/3.4.1/css/bootstrap.min.css">
<script src="https://ajax.googleapis.com/ajax/libs/jquery/3.7.1/jquery.min.js"></script>
<script src="https://maxcdn.bootstrapcdn.com/bootstrap/3.4.1/js/bootstrap.min.js"></script>
```
What is the role of these three lines?

c.x: The `<link>` loads jQuery, and the two `<script>` tags load Bootstrap's CSS and JavaScript
The `<link>` loads Bootstrap's CSS, and the two `<script>` tags load jQuery and Bootstrap's JavaScript
The `<link>` loads Bootstrap's JavaScript, and the two `<script>` tags load jQuery and Bootstrap's CSS
The `<link>` and the first `<script>` load Bootstrap's CSS, and the last `<script>` loads jQuery

qs.e: The `<link>` tag points to `bootstrap.min.css` (the styles). The first `<script>` loads jQuery, and the last `<script>` loads Bootstrap's JavaScript file `bootstrap.min.js`.

qs.q: The lecture's CDN example loads jQuery before `bootstrap.min.js` (version 3.4.1). Which statement explains why this is needed?

c.x: jQuery is needed only to make the layout responsive on small phones
jQuery is required for every Bootstrap version, including Bootstrap 5
Bootstrap 3 relies on jQuery, which Bootstrap 5 replaced with plain JavaScript
Bootstrap 3 relies on jQuery, and Bootstrap 5 also needs it for its CSS files

qs.e: The lecture says Bootstrap 5 switched to JavaScript instead of jQuery, which means Bootstrap 3 (the version used in the example, 3.4.1) depends on jQuery. That is why the jQuery script is included before `bootstrap.min.js`.

qs.q: A developer downloads Bootstrap from getbootstrap.com instead of using a CDN. What must be done next to use it in a page?

c.x: Nothing, because the browser detects the downloaded files automatically
Convert the downloaded files into a CDN link before using them
Rename the downloaded files to `.html` so the page can load them
Link the downloaded Bootstrap files in the HTML page

qs.e: The second way to use Bootstrap is to download its files from getbootstrap.com and <u>link them</u> in your HTML page, just like any other CSS and JavaScript files.

qs.q: The same Bootstrap page looks good on a small phone and on a large desktop, without building separate versions. Which feature is mainly responsible?

c.x: Its optional JavaScript plugins, which download a different page for each device
Its responsive CSS, which adjusts the layout to the screen size
Its CDN, which detects the device and replaces the HTML file
Its download package, which contains one page per device type

qs.e: Bootstrap's responsive CSS adjusts automatically to phones, tablets, and desktops. This is what responsive web design means: one site that looks good on all devices.
